title: Hiring Panel Design and Manager Interview Navigator
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This guide defines Redwood Inference's recommended design for hiring panels and a practical interviewer navigator for manager-level interviews (IC→manager transitions and new manager hires). It focuses on equitable, time-efficient panels that surface leadership potential, role fit, and operational readiness while producing consistent decisions and clean handoffs to onboarding and people-ops workflows.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce variance in manager hiring outcomes, speed decision velocity, and ensure fair assessment across distributed interview panels.
- Scope: Applies to all people-ops, engineering, product, and go-to-market manager hires at Redwood. This document complements the company scorecard and hiring committee protocols.

Why panels matter for manager hires:
1) Signal diversity: multiple interviewers reduce single-interviewer bias.
2) Cross-functional validation: managers must partner with product, infra, GTM, and people-ops. Panels ensure upstream/downstream stakeholders see the candidate.
3) Operational readiness: beyond technical ability, managers need planning, hiring cadence instincts, and a clear approach to 1:1s, feedback, and escalation. Panels explicitly validate these domains.

Panel composition (recommended templates):
- Core panel (standard 4 people, 60–75 minutes total):
  - Hiring manager (or cross-team peer lead) — 20 minutes — owns role-context and team fit assessment
  - People Ops interviewer — 10–15 minutes — assesses compensation/expectations alignment, inclusivity, and risk flags
  - Functional peer — 10–15 minutes — assesses day-to-day collaboration and technical/process fit
  - Leadership/skip-level partner — 15–20 minutes — assesses strategy, coaching instincts, and escalation judgment

- Expanded panel (optional, 90 minutes): add one of:
  - Direct report simulation (senior IC) — evaluates delegation & hiring lens
  - Cross-functional partner (product/infra/security) — for roles with heavy cross-team responsibilities

Role definitions and responsibilities:
- Panel owner (typically the hiring manager or interviewing manager): schedule, collect scorecards, run post-interview debrief, and submit recommendation.
- People Ops interviewer: triages red flags, clarifies compensation expectations, and ensures compliance with interview laws and diversity commitments.
- Interviewers: prepare questions tied to the scorecard, submit written notes within 24 hours, and attend the debrief when requested.

Interviewer preparation checklist (to be completed 24–48 hours in advance):
1) Read candidate resume and cover letter; highlight three clarifying questions.
2) Review the role scorecard and identify which competencies you will evaluate.
3) Confirm time-boxed areas for the interview and share structure with candidate at the start.
4) Read diversity and bias-awareness reminders (2-minute primer attached).

Scorecard and evaluation rubric (single-page canonical):
- Competencies (rate 1–5 with evidence notes):
  - Role-specific execution (deliverables & planning)
  - Team leadership & coaching (feedback examples)
  - Hiring and talent judgment (sourcing/assessment approach)
  - Cross-functional partnership (stakeholder management)
  - Operational rigor & escalation (on-call/incident examples)
  - Cultural values alignment (examples aligned to Redwood values)
- Overall recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / Consider with reservations / No hire
- Must-have checklist (Y/N): any legal, security, or compliance blockers recorded here (e.g., conflicts of interest, export control risk).

Sample interviewer questions (by competency):
- Role-specific execution: "Walk me through a recent quarter where your team missed a goal. How did you diagnose root cause, reprioritize work, and communicate the outcome?"
- Team leadership & coaching: "Tell me about a direct report who stalled on growth. What was your plan, how did you change it, and what happened?"
- Hiring and talent judgment: "How do you decide between hiring a junior engineer now vs. contracting for capacity? Give a recent example with metrics or milestones."
- Cross-functional partnership: "Describe a time you disagreed with a product tradeoff. How did you raise concerns and what was the final outcome?"
- Operational rigor: "Describe a production incident where you coordinated across teams. What was your role and what process changes did you implement afterward?"
- Values & fit: "What role should a manager play in shaping a team’s rituals and culture? Give a concrete example of something you changed."

Interview flow and timeboxing recommendations (60-minute core panel):
- 0:00–03:00 — welcome, role framing by hiring manager (candidate questions about context)
- 03:00–25:00 — hiring manager deep dive (execution & planning)
- 25:00–35:00 — functional peer (technical/process fit)
- 35:00–50:00 — leadership/skip-level partner (strategy & coaching)
- 50:00–60:00 — people-ops (compensation, expectations, candidate questions)
- Post-interview: each interviewer adds notes to scorecard (within 24 hours) and shares availability for a 15-minute debrief (within 48 hours).

Debrief and decision protocol (fast, equitable):
1) Convene panel owner + people-ops + at least two interviewers within 48 hours.
2) Review scorecards, escalate any must-have fails, and surface any conflicting signals.
3) Use structured decision rubric: if 3+ interviewers mark "Strong hire" or 2 "Strong" + 1 "Hire" → recommend offer. If split across categories, escalate to hiring committee for tie-break.
4) Document decision rationale in the candidate record (two-paragraph summary) and next steps (offer, second-stage assignment, or reject).

Bias mitigation and equity checkpoints:
- Use the same core scorecard across all candidates for a role.
- At least one interviewer should be from a different team to reduce mirror-hiring bias.
- People Ops must confirm compensation band alignment before an offer.
- Avoid “culture fit” language; instead use “values alignment” with explicit behavioral examples.

Legal, compliance, and international hiring considerations:
- Do not ask about protected characteristics. People Ops provides a one-page country-specific question checklist for remote hires; consult it before finalizing interview panels when the candidate is located outside the US.
- For roles requiring export-controlled work, include Security reviewer in the panel and add relevant yes/no checkpoints to the scorecard.

Handoff to onboarding (people-ops + hiring manager):
1) If offer accepted, hiring manager populates the manager onboarding intake within 24 hours: team goals, 30/60/90 expectations, access matrix, and first-month meeting plan.
2) People Ops schedules a Manager Onboarding Kickoff within first week (includes benefits, payroll, compliance, culture).
3) Assign a peer buddy for the first 90 days and include cross-functional onboarding sessions.

Feedback templates and candidate communication (timely, transparent):
- Rejection message (within 5 business days): brief strengths, one area for growth, and encouragement to reapply if appropriate.
- Offer message: link to offer doc, role expectations, manager onboarding timeline, and people-ops contact.

Measuring panel effectiveness (KPIs to track):
- Time-to-decision (target: median ≤ 7 days post-final interview)
- Offer-accept rate (target: ≥ 65% for manager roles)
- Hiring quality (90-day manager effectiveness scorecard: onboarding completion, direct reports' early feedback)
- Panel calibration score (quarterly review of score distributions and decision variance)

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Pitfall: overloaded hiring managers delaying debriefs → Mitigation: auto-escalate to hiring committee if no decision within 10 days.
- Pitfall: inconsistent scorecard use → Mitigation: require at least one structured comment per competency before debrief.
- Pitfall: late compensation surprises → Mitigation: mandatory People Ops pre-filtering step.

Manager interviewer playbook (quick-actions):
- Before: read scorecard, prepare 3 behavior-based questions, block 15 minutes after the interview for notes.
- During: timebox, invite candidate to ask 2 questions at the end, look for coaching examples.
- After: add evidence-backed rating and a concise rationale sentence; flag any red flags immediately to People Ops.

Appendix A — Example single-page scorecard (text template):
- Candidate name: ____________
- Role: ____________
- Interviewer: ____________
- Date: ____________
- Competency ratings (1–5) + 1-sentence evidence per competency
- Overall recommendation (Strong Hire / Hire / Consider / No Hire)
- Must-have blockers: [list]
- Free notes (2–3 bullets)

Appendix B — Debrief checklist (15 minutes):
1) Read aloud overall recommendation from each interviewer (30s each)
2) Confirm any must-have fails (Y/N)
3) Discuss 1 strength and 1 concern (5 minutes)
4) Vote and record rationale (team consensus or escalate)
5) Confirm next step and ownership for candidate communication

Appendix C — Short bias-awareness primer (to attach to interview invites):
- Reminders: avoid confirming questions that probe protected characteristics; focus on behavior, outcomes, and tradeoffs; note gut impressions but ground ratings in examples.

Maintenance and governance:
- People-ops will review this guide annually and after any significant hiring committee decision.
- Quarterly calibration sessions will sample 10 manager hiring files for review; results feed a continuous-improvement backlog.
